title: 50/30/20 Budgeting Rule — A Simple Framework for Young Earners
publisher: RBI Financial Literacy Portal (RBI kehta hai)
text: The 50/30/20 rule is a simple budgeting guideline popular among young earners. It divides your monthly take-home income into three buckets: 50% for Needs (essentials), 30% for Wants (lifestyle), and 20% for Savings and investments. Needs (50%): Rent, groceries, utilities, transportation to work, healthcare, loan EMIs, insurance premiums — things you cannot avoid. If your needs exceed 50%, look for ways to reduce fixed costs (share accommodation, use public transport). Wants (30%): Dining out, streaming subscriptions, shopping, entertainment, travel, gadgets — things you enjoy but can live without. This is where most overspending happens. Savings (20%): Putting money aside before spending — in a savings account, PPF, mutual fund SIP, or emergency fund. Financial experts suggest building an emergency fund of 3–6 months of expenses before investing. Important note: The 50/30/20 rule is a guideline, not a rigid rule. In high-rent cities like Mumbai or Bangalore, needs may take 60–65% of income for young earners. The goal is to increase savings over time. Even starting at 10% and increasing by 1–2% every year (the Save More Tomorrow / SMarT approach) builds strong financial habits.
